title: Functoriality of the Cech-to-cohomology diagram along a morphism of ringed spaces
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter cohomology.tex (Cohomology of Sheaves), section on the Cech complex
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma attaches to a morphism of ringed spaces f : X -> Y, an f-map phi : f^*G -> F and coverings U of X refining f^{-1}V a commutative diagram in D^+(O_X(X)) between the Cech complexes and derived global sections, together with its consequence for cohomology groups (statement lines 2521-2552). The proof has to build the arrow rather than invoke it: a choice function c : I -> J with U_i contained in f^{-1}(V_{c(i)}) defines gamma in every degree (proof lines 2556-2564), and then four double complexes A^{bullet,bullet}, B^{bullet,bullet}, (B')^{bullet,bullet}, (B'')^{bullet,bullet} have to be introduced, the last one using the f-map f_*I^bullet -> I^bullet, together with a third injective resolution f_*I -> (J')^bullet and a morphism beta making equation-choice commute (proof lines 2565-2591). The remaining work is the bookkeeping of the displayed diagram: which shapes commute, and why the two outer routes from Cech^bullet(V,G) to Gamma(X, I^bullet) agree after inverting quasi-isomorphisms (proof lines 2617-2629). The specific difficulty is that these double complexes are not defined in the counted statement but only inside the proof of the Cech-to-cohomology comparison, so two injective resolutions plus a third one for f_*I^bullet have to be kept coherent at once while every square of the diagram is checked. The claim is H2.
